description.short: Smooth black tea from the home of what was once the largest state tea farm in the USSR
description.overview: The settlement of Dagomys was the industrial heartland of Soviet tea production, making its name synonymous with domestic tea for an entire generation.
description.taste: Soft, gentle black tea typical of the northern Caucasian terroir

history.origin: The Dagomys State Tea Farm was founded in the Soviet period as one of the flagship enterprises for industrial domestic tea production.
history.development: At its peak, the enterprise supplied a major portion of the country's domestic tea demand, making Krasnodar tea from Dagomys a household name.
history.modern: Following the collapse of the Soviet Union, production contracted significantly, but the Dagomys name remains culturally iconic for older generations.
interestingFacts: In Soviet times, Dagomys State Tea Farm served as an official showcase site where foreign delegations were brought to witness the achievements of northern subtropical agriculture.
For many in Russia, 'Dagomys' became a colloquial synonym for domestic tea in general, regardless of the exact plantation of origin.
